answer: Whether an agent sells willow seedlings or ocean forecasts, each seller identity must lock a fixed bond before bidding, with funds held for 30 days after its last job. An audit thread links each bid to its bond, so one deposit cannot back several identities at once. Creating 1,000 fake sellers requires 1,000 bonds, tying up capital for the lock period; identities remain cheap to invent but costly to activate.
